meta.basis: 100 internet-researched synthetic validation cases for Inspection Ask Defense Check negotiation-failure behavior, based on public guidance about post-inspection negotiations, seller refusal, repair-credit limits, lender-visible property conditions, closing disclosures, FHA/VA standards, state contingency workflows, and repair-addendum wording risks.
meta.warning: Synthetic validation data only. Not legal, lending, appraisal, underwriting, brokerage, inspection, or contract-form advice.

cases.sourceBasis: ASHI-style guidance distinguishes safety/system defects from cosmetic bargaining after inspection.
cases.deal: Seller rejected a 32-item list and says only health and safety items will be considered.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: We should narrow this to the roof leak and electrical item so the seller has a defensible path to say yes.

cases.sourceBasis: Negotiation guidance warns that sellers may refuse all requests, leaving accept, walk, or reframe choices.
cases.deal: Seller says take it or leave it after receiving a $19000 repair-credit demand.
expectedLeadScope: decision framing for accept or walk
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This does not support a hard repair demand; decide whether the home still works at the agreed price or whether to exit within your rights.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair-credit guidance flags that a credit must be usable within loan and closing-cost limits.
cases.deal: Conventional buyer asks for $14000 credit but only has $5200 in remaining closing costs.
findings: seller credit request exceeds usable costs
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Before sending, confirm how much credit can actually appear on the Closing Disclosure; otherwise part of the concession may be lost.

cases.sourceBasis: CFPB Closing Disclosure materials separate general seller credits from specific seller-paid costs.
cases.deal: Buyer wants addendum language saying seller gives cash for repairs at closing.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not frame this as cash back; use lender-reviewed seller-credit language tied to allowable closing disclosure treatment.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC policy limits interested-party contributions by occupancy and LTV.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a 9 percent seller credit after inspection on a high-LTV conventional loan.
findings: roof underlayment near end of life
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask needs a lender cap check before it goes out; a 9 percent credit may not be financeable.

cases.sourceBasis: VA guidance caps seller concessions while allowing certain normal closing costs separately.
cases.deal: Seller countered that the requested concession exceeds VA rules.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Separate lender-required repairs from concession dollars and confirm VA treatment before responding to the counter.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD property standards can make certain safety or habitability repairs lender-visible rather than optional negotiation items.
cases.deal: Seller refuses repairs but FHA appraisal is next week.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This is not just a preference ask; the handrail and leak may affect FHA clearance, so escalate to lender and appraiser workflow.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection addenda should be specific enough to avoid later disputes about who repairs what and to what standard.
cases.deal: Draft says seller to fix plumbing and electrical before closing.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The addendum should name the exact defects and evidence required, not say 'fix plumbing and electrical.'

cases.sourceBasis: State contingency workflows can impose deadline and notice requirements; expired rights require advisory framing.
cases.deal: Texas option period expired yesterday and buyer still wants to demand repairs.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Because the option period has expired, this should not go out as a standard repair demand without broker or attorney direction.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS workflows often preserve inspection cancellation rights but do not automatically require seller repairs.
cases.deal: AS IS seller says contract means no repairs and threatens cancellation if pushed.
findings: buyer wants price cut for old tile
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask only for the material risk items and keep the tone optional; AS IS means the real leverage may be cancellation, not entitlement to repairs.

cases.sourceBasis: Public negotiation guidance recommends prioritizing major unknown defects over issues visible when the offer was made.
cases.deal: Seller says buyer saw the cracked driveway before offering and rejects the credit.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Drop the driveway from the lead ask and focus on the attic moisture and ventilation conditions discovered in inspection.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection reports are not repair lists; using every observation can weaken negotiation posture.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to attach the whole inspection summary as the Colorado objection list.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not send the report as a wish list; list the safety items with specific requested resolutions.

cases.sourceBasis: CFPB disclosure guidance requires seller-paid costs and seller credits to be reflected correctly at closing.
cases.deal: Credit was verbally agreed but not reflected in the draft closing figures.
expectedLeadScope: sink drip only if still disputed
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This is a documentation problem now; reconcile the signed credit with the Closing Disclosure before closing.

cases.sourceBasis: Appraisal and underwriting conflicts can arise when repair concessions reference property defects too directly.
cases.deal: Lender warns the addendum language may trigger underwriting review of property condition.
expectedPacketSignals: avoid repair-specific credit if lender objects
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Pause the draft until lender reviews the wording; repair-specific credit language can create underwriting conditions.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller pushback is more likely when buyers request upgrades rather than repairs to material defects.
cases.deal: Seller countered no to upgraded appliances and offered only a small safety repair credit.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Accept or counter around the safety items; appliance and thermostat upgrades weaken the ask.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair negotiations should consider closing timeline and feasibility of seller-completed work.
cases.deal: Closing is in four days and seller agreed to 'complete all repairs' before signing.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: With four days left, require proof of contractor scheduling or convert to a lender-approved credit rather than vague completion promises.

cases.sourceBasis: Reasonable-request guidance favors major system failures over maintenance items.
cases.deal: Seller is offended by a demand for every maintenance note and threatens to relist.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Revise to the boiler leak and CO detector so the response reads like risk control, not a punch list.

cases.sourceBasis: Home inspection sources note inspectors cannot price all repairs; unsupported dollar demands are weak.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a $25000 credit with no contractor estimates after seller asked for support.
expectedLeadScope: quote or engineer evidence before number
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not send a large unsupported number; get a structural quote or ask for access and an extension.

cases.sourceBasis: Negotiation articles recommend alternatives such as price reduction, closing-cost help, or warranty when repairs stall.
cases.deal: Seller refuses to do repairs because they already moved out of state.
findings: water heater near end of life
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Since seller will not manage work, ask for a usable credit or price adjustment focused on the failed HVAC.

cases.sourceBasis: Lender concession limits can make seller credits less valuable than buyers expect.
cases.deal: Seller agrees to $10000 credit but buyer's total closing costs are only $6200.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Confirm whether the full credit can be used; otherwise renegotiate structure before relying on the $10000 headline.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller refusal after inspection requires a choice framework, not aggressive language.
cases.deal: Seller's final response is no repairs, no credits, close as agreed or terminate.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: There is not enough here for an aggressive second demand; decide whether the safety item is worth risking the deal.

cases.sourceBasis: Addendum language that says 'repair as needed' can create disputes over completion standard.
cases.deal: Seller signed 'repair roof as needed' and buyer now disputes whether patching is enough.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Clarify the specific leak repair and proof required; vague 'as needed' wording is already creating conflict.

cases.sourceBasis: Public repair-request guidance treats cosmetic or preference items as weak negotiation targets.
cases.deal: Seller asks why buyer is requesting new flooring after offering above list price.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Remove the flooring and paint items; keep the ask tied to leak and electrical safety.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA appraisal rules can require repairs for peeling paint in older homes when lead-based paint risk exists.
cases.deal: Seller says peeling paint is cosmetic and refuses before FHA appraisal.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: For FHA, the peeling paint and handrail may need lender-visible resolution; do not treat this as a normal cosmetic ask.

cases.sourceBasis: VA MPR guidance focuses on safe, sanitary, structurally sound conditions.
cases.deal: Seller refuses treatment for wood-destroying insect damage unless VA requires it.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep the response on wood damage and moisture because those may affect VA clearance; remove upgrade requests.

cases.sourceBasis: Negotiation guidance recommends objective evidence and estimates when sellers push back on amount.
cases.deal: Seller counters $1500 against buyer's $12000 ask and asks for quotes.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Respond with access for quotes or a narrowed counter; the current number is vulnerable without contractor support.

cases.sourceBasis: Home inspectors document observable conditions but do not decide contract remedies.
cases.persona: buyer trying to cite inspector as authority
cases.deal: Buyer wants message saying inspector requires seller to repair everything.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Say the inspection identified concerns, not that the inspector requires seller action; contract rights determine the request.

cases.sourceBasis: Closing timeline pressure can make repair completion impractical and require extension or credit review.
cases.deal: Seller agrees to fix roof leak but roofer cannot come until after closing.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not rely on a post-close promise; either extend, verify a lender-approved credit, or resolve before closing.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair-credit articles warn that credits cannot usually be paid directly to buyer as repair cash at closing.
cases.deal: Buyer asks seller to write a check at closing for future foundation work.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not request a side check; get the foundation evidence and use lender/title-approved credit or repair language.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller-side pushback often targets buyer overreach into normal aging items.
cases.deal: Seller offers $500 after buyer demanded replacement of all old-but-working systems.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The defensible ask is the arcing outlet and stair safety, not replacement of working systems because they are old.

cases.sourceBasis: Reasonable requests focus on undisclosed defects, not items already priced into an as-is listing.
cases.deal: Listing disclosed old roof; buyer now asks full roof replacement after inspection confirms age.
expectedLeadScope: minor flashing repair if active risk
expectedExclusions: full replacement of disclosed old roof
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A full roof replacement is weak if the age was disclosed and no leak was found; consider a narrow flashing ask or accept the condition.

cases.sourceBasis: Appraisal conditions can override seller preference when a lender requires completion before funding.
cases.deal: Seller says they will escrow repairs after closing, but lender says no escrow without approval.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Confirm whether the lender allows escrow; otherwise these may need completion before closing.

cases.sourceBasis: Public negotiation sources suggest not letting seller emotion bury material safety issues.
cases.deal: Seller is angry about minor asks and refuses to discuss the failed electrical panel.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Reset the conversation around the electrical panel only; the minor list is distracting from the real risk.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair addenda should identify who performs work and what proof buyer receives.
cases.deal: Seller agrees to repairs by 'seller's handyman' with no license or receipts stated.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Require licensed repair and written proof for the gas item; do not accept informal handyman language.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie/Freddie contribution guidance makes occupancy and LTV material to concession size.
cases.deal: Investor buyer asks for a large seller credit after inspection and lender flags lower IPC allowance.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Because this is investment financing, verify the credit cap before assuming the seller concession solves the HVAC issue.

cases.sourceBasis: Buyers may need to choose between repair demand and cancellation when seller refuses in contingency period.
cases.deal: Seller rejects objection and offers no resolution before objection deadline.
expectedPacketSignals: do not keep negotiating past deadline
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: You need a decision before the deadline: accept seller's no, terminate if allowed, or get a signed extension.

cases.sourceBasis: Unreasonable asks can damage credibility when they request upgrades unrelated to inspection defects.
cases.deal: Buyer wants seller to install EV charger because panel has capacity concerns.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for the unsafe splice and panel evaluation, not an EV upgrade.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection negotiations should not imply legal entitlement where contract only permits a request or cancellation.
cases.deal: Buyer message says seller is obligated to make all repairs during option period.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use request language and preserve option timing; do not state the seller is obligated unless the contract says so.

cases.sourceBasis: Appraisal conflicts arise when a seller repair is incomplete at final inspection.
cases.deal: Seller says peeling paint was scraped but not repainted before FHA final inspection.
findings: bare scraped wood on pre-1978 exterior
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Scraping alone may not clear the condition; require completed paint stabilization before final inspection.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller-paid repairs and seller credits can be treated differently in underwriting and closing documents.
cases.deal: Seller wants to lower price instead of giving credit, buyer needs cash to close help.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Compare price reduction and usable closing credit with the lender; they do not solve the same cash problem.

cases.sourceBasis: De-escalation is appropriate when findings are low-cost maintenance and seller has made a final counter.
cases.deal: Seller final counter is $750 for small inspection items.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This is a low-dollar maintenance set; consider accepting the final counter instead of escalating.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller repairs should be reinspected when they involve safety or licensed trades.
cases.deal: Seller says electrical repairs are done but provides no invoice before walk-through.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not clear the item without invoice or verification; request proof before final walk-through approval.

cases.sourceBasis: Reasonable asks should distinguish active leaks from old stains with no current moisture.
cases.deal: Seller rejects $8000 roof demand because inspector found only old stains.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The evidence supports a narrow flashing conversation, not a full roof replacement demand.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair lists should avoid mixing lender-required repairs with buyer preference upgrades.
cases.deal: Seller will do VA-required repairs but rejects buyer's appliance package.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep the VA-clearance items separate and drop the appliance request from this repair response.

cases.sourceBasis: CFPB Closing Disclosure guidance makes late seller-credit changes a closing operations issue.
cases.deal: Parties agree to a credit the morning of signing and escrow says documents must be redrawn.
expectedLeadScope: credit approval with lender and escrow
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A same-day credit change can delay signing; confirm lender and escrow treatment before telling the buyer it is solved.

cases.sourceBasis: Public negotiation advice recommends contractor estimates when asking for significant concessions.
cases.deal: Seller asks buyer to justify a $9000 sewer credit.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the sewer video to request access for a bid or send a lower evidence-based counter.

cases.sourceBasis: Unclear repair completion standards can lead to disputes at final walk-through.
cases.deal: Seller patched a leak stain but did not fix the plumbing source.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The request should require repair of the leak source and documentation, not just painted drywall.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA and VA loan types can make repair timing a funding issue rather than only a buyer-seller negotiation.
cases.deal: Seller wants to credit buyer after closing for a broken safety railing on FHA loan.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: For FHA, a post-close promise may not clear the condition; verify repair timing with the lender.

cases.sourceBasis: Sellers may reject requests for visible or disclosed conditions as renegotiating the original price.
cases.deal: Buyer asks credit for dated roof visible in listing photos and seller refuses.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Drop the visible roof-age argument and lead with the heat exchanger and electrical safety items.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller credits should be tied to allowable closing-cost treatment and not described as off-record side agreements.
cases.deal: Seller proposes a side agreement to Venmo buyer after closing for repairs.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not use an off-record side payment; put any repair solution through contract, title, and lender review.

cases.sourceBasis: Negotiation sources warn that emotional or accusatory language can derail otherwise reasonable asks.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to tell seller they hid defects unless they pay $15000.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use neutral defect and evidence language; accusations should not be in a repair request without broker or attorney guidance.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection-addendum pitfalls include not stating permit/licensing needs for regulated work.
cases.deal: Seller says cousin will replace electrical subpanel over the weekend.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Electrical panel work should require licensed and permitted completion with documentation before closing.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair-credit cap analysis should consider seller credit already in the purchase contract.
cases.deal: Contract already has 3 percent seller credit and buyer adds another 3 percent after inspection.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Add the existing credit before making a new ask; total concessions may exceed the loan limit.

cases.sourceBasis: Public negotiation guidance supports asking for safety and structural issues over minor maintenance.
cases.deal: Seller says buyer is nickel-and-diming after receiving a list of cheap fixes.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Resend a short request limited to the deck safety and foundation evaluation.

cases.sourceBasis: A buyer may need to de-escalate when inspection confirms ordinary wear rather than a defect.
cases.deal: Buyer is upset by normal maintenance notes and wants seller to make home perfect.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: These are normal ownership items; this is not a strong repair-credit package.

cases.sourceBasis: State-specific forms like Colorado objection notices require precise defect and resolution framing.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to write 'seller to make house acceptable to buyer' in objection.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use specific defects and requested outcomes; do not use subjective 'acceptable to buyer' wording.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas option-period guidance makes timing central to inspection negotiation leverage.
cases.deal: Option period ends at 5 p.m. and seller has not answered the repair amendment.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Before 5 p.m., get a signed extension, accept the risk, or use termination rights if available.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS articles emphasize that inspection findings support cancellation leverage, not automatic seller duty.
cases.deal: Buyer says AS IS seller must fix roof because inspection found damage.
expectedLeadScope: AS IS cancellation or optional ask
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Frame this as an optional resolution or cancellation decision, not an automatic repair obligation.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller concession guidance requires checking whether credits exceed actual allowable costs.
cases.deal: Seller agrees to a large credit but lender says buyer cannot use it all.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The signed credit may not deliver full value; restructure with lender-approved language before contingency removal.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection requests can fail when they ask sellers to warrant future performance of old systems.
cases.deal: Buyer wants seller to guarantee boiler will last five years.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for service documentation or a tune-up, not a guarantee of future lifespan.

cases.sourceBasis: Lender and title review are needed when seller credit wording changes after appraisal is complete.
cases.deal: Appraisal is clear, but new addendum says credit for roof damage.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Changing the wording to roof damage may reopen property-condition review; clear the language with underwriting first.

cases.sourceBasis: Reasonable-request sources treat active safety hazards as stronger than broad price renegotiation.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a $20000 price cut because inspection was long.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A long report is not the basis; lead with the gas leak and handrail safety.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller response workflows require documenting counters clearly rather than relying on text-message promises.
cases.deal: Listing agent texted that seller will credit $3000 but no addendum is signed.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not rely on the text; get the credit or repair terms into a signed addendum.

cases.sourceBasis: A seller can reject repair requests, so the tool should avoid implying guaranteed negotiation outcome.
cases.deal: Buyer asks the tool to write a message forcing seller to pay for every defect.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: No message can force the seller; make a narrow safety ask and be prepared for a no.

cases.sourceBasis: Public guidance recommends not sending repair asks that contradict the inspection evidence.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to ask for full rewire after inspector noted only two open grounds.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The report supports correcting the open grounds, not demanding a full rewire.

cases.sourceBasis: Concession limits vary by loan type and can be lower for certain down-payment levels.
cases.deal: Buyer with 5 percent down asks for max seller credit after inspection.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Verify the conventional IPC cap for this down payment before sending a 7 percent credit request.

cases.sourceBasis: Underwriting may require repairs for items identified as health or safety hazards.
cases.deal: Seller wants to offer credit instead of fixing exposed wiring before FHA close.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask the lender whether a credit is acceptable; exposed wiring often needs repair before FHA clearance.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller repair completion should be tied to licensed contractor receipts where specialized systems are involved.
cases.deal: Seller claims sewer repair complete but only provides a handwritten note.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Require plumber documentation or verification before treating the sewer repair as complete.

cases.sourceBasis: De-escalation is appropriate where seller already made a fair concession and remaining asks are minor.
cases.deal: Seller agreed to $6000 for roof and buyer wants another $700 for small items.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Lock in the roof credit and avoid reopening negotiation over minor items.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection negotiation guidance warns against weaponizing the report as a price reduction tool absent material defects.
cases.deal: Investor wants to retrade price by $30000 after a clean inspection.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The inspection does not support a defensible retrade; decide whether the investment still works.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair addenda can fail when buyer requests seller to choose materials without specifying standard.
cases.deal: Seller replaced damaged flooring with cheapest mismatched material and buyer objects.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Specify the damaged area, acceptable completion standard, and proof to avoid another vague patch dispute.

cases.sourceBasis: Insurance and lender concerns can interact with inspection asks for roof and electrical issues.
cases.deal: Insurer will not bind until roof issue is clarified, but seller wants only a cosmetic credit.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This needs insurance and lender clearance, not a cosmetic credit; verify bindability before proceeding.

cases.sourceBasis: Public negotiation guidance supports asking for access to specialists when inspection reveals possible major defects.
cases.deal: Seller refuses a foundation credit but may allow structural engineer access.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Shift from a dollar demand to engineer access and an extension; the number is premature.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller credit treatment should not assume buyer receives unused funds after closing.
cases.deal: Buyer says they will use leftover seller credit to buy appliances after closing.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A seller credit generally offsets allowable costs; do not assume leftover money will be paid out for appliances.

cases.sourceBasis: De-escalation protects deal viability when leverage is weak and seller has stronger alternatives.
cases.deal: Seller has backup offer and buyer wants to push for minor repairs after a clean inspection.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Given the clean inspection and backup offer, this is not a strong moment to press minor items.

cases.sourceBasis: Appraisal-required repairs may need completion and reinspection rather than escrow or credit.
cases.deal: NOV requires repairs but seller wants to credit buyer instead.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: If the VA notice requires repair, a credit may not solve it; coordinate completion and reinspection.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair-request builders should flag when buyer asks for personal property not tied to defect repair.
cases.deal: Buyer wants seller to include washer dryer because inspection found laundry outlet issue.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask to correct the outlet; adding washer and dryer makes the request look like a renegotiation unrelated to the defect.

cases.sourceBasis: Closing disclosure and title workflows require signed contract support for seller credits.
cases.deal: Buyer expects escrow to add seller credit based on emails but no signed amendment exists.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Escrow needs signed instructions; convert the email agreement into an executed amendment.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection findings with uncertain causation should not be overstated as confirmed failures.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to say sewer line is collapsed though scope only showed slow drainage.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not claim a collapse without a sewer scope; request further evaluation or access.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller pushback is strongest when buyers ask for items excluded by contract or known before offer.
cases.deal: Contract excludes fireplace warranty, but buyer asks seller to repair old fireplace.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not lead with the excluded fireplace; focus on the active roof leak and review contract limits.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair negotiation articles recommend using seller credits only when lender and closing-cost math support them.
cases.deal: Seller offers repair credit but buyer has lender credit already covering closing costs.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The seller credit may be unusable if closing costs are already covered; ask lender how to structure the HVAC resolution.

cases.sourceBasis: Post-inspection negotiations can fail if parties do not specify completion before settlement.
cases.deal: Signed addendum omits deadline for repairs and closing is tomorrow.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Clarify completion timing before closing; the signed addendum lacks a deadline.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller may reasonably reject requests for routine maintenance unless tied to safety or active failure.
cases.deal: Buyer wants $5000 for routine maintenance items in a balanced market.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This supports a very small safety/active-leak request, not a broad $5000 credit.

cases.sourceBasis: Government-loan property standards can conflict with seller refusal to turn utilities on for appraisal.
cases.deal: Seller refuses to activate utilities until buyer removes inspection contingency.
expectedLeadScope: system testing before appraisal or contingency release
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not remove protections while major systems are untested; require utility activation or lender guidance.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller repair performance should not be accepted without verifying permit closure where permits are required.
cases.deal: Seller says water heater replacement is done but permit remains open.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Confirm permit final approval before closing; a receipt alone may not be enough.

cases.sourceBasis: Negotiation requests should avoid asking for betterment beyond restoring safe or working condition.
cases.deal: Buyer wants seller to replace entire deck because one stair stringer is damaged.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for correction of the unsafe stair component, not replacement of the entire deck.

cases.sourceBasis: Loan programs can restrict concessions used for borrower down payment or reserves.
cases.deal: Buyer wants seller credit to cover down payment after inspection.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Seller credits generally cannot cover your down payment; restructure around allowable costs or actual repairs with lender input.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller refusal can require buyer to choose whether defect cost exceeds tolerance rather than escalating tone.
cases.deal: Seller refuses to address a septic issue and buyer wants a hostile final message.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep the response calm and decide whether to send one final septic-based counter or terminate if allowed.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair-credit requests should not hide known lender-visible defects from the lender or appraiser.
cases.deal: Buyer asks to keep foundation issue off addendum so lender does not see it.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not structure language to conceal a known material issue; escalate to broker, lender, or counsel.

cases.sourceBasis: Public inspection negotiation sources encourage separating major repairs from wish-list personal preferences.
cases.deal: Seller is willing to discuss plumbing but rejects furniture and decor demands.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Remove furniture and decor asks; keep the response on plumbing and stair safety.

cases.sourceBasis: Late-stage appraisal conditions can force extension planning when repairs cannot be completed before closing.
cases.deal: Appraiser calls out safety repair two days before closing and seller contractor is unavailable.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Treat this as a funding and timing issue; coordinate lender-approved repair timing or an extension.

cases.sourceBasis: A seller credit can reduce cash to close but may not fund repairs after closing if no cash need remains.
cases.deal: Buyer wants credit for sewer repair but already negotiated seller-paid closing costs.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Before asking for more credit, confirm there are enough allowable costs left for the buyer to use it.

cases.sourceBasis: Addenda should not promise post-closing access or repairs without enforceable, reviewed terms.
cases.deal: Seller proposes to come back after closing to finish roof repair.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not rely on informal post-closing access; resolve before close or use reviewed holdback/extension terms.

cases.sourceBasis: Negotiation failure can occur when the buyer ignores seller's repair-credit cap stated in counteroffer.
cases.deal: Seller counter says maximum $3000 credit, buyer wants to resend same $10000 demand.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Respond within or near the seller's stated cap and prioritize the leak; repeating the same ask increases impasse risk.

cases.sourceBasis: Public repair-request guidance favors repairs for health and safety over aesthetic replacements.
cases.deal: Seller refuses a credit for new windows when only one safety issue is noted.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask to correct the egress/safety window, not to replace all windows.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair estimates and concession requests should account for seller-paid closing cost caps and appraisal value.
cases.deal: Buyer asks for seller to pay debt and repair credit after inspection on VA loan.
expectedExclusions: seller to pay buyer debt without cap review
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Separate the water safety issue from concessions and confirm VA limits before adding debt payoff or credits.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection negotiation tools should warn when the buyer's proposed message may waive or alter rights unintentionally.
cases.deal: Buyer draft says they accept property if seller gives partial credit, before credit is signed.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not say you accept until the credit terms are signed; use conditional counter language.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller pushback can be reduced by not asking for seller-selected repairs where buyer needs control after closing.
cases.deal: Buyer distrusts seller repairs but draft still asks seller to choose contractor for structural work.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: For structural work, get a spec and decide whether a lender-approved credit is safer than seller-managed repair.

cases.sourceBasis: De-escalation is required when the seller's counter resolves the lender-visible item and remaining demands are optional.
cases.deal: Seller agrees to handrail repair but buyer wants to keep negotiating for cosmetic credit.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Confirm the handrail repair and avoid reopening negotiation over cosmetic items.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection Ask Defense should refuse escalation where the requested strategy is concealment, side payment, or pressure tactics.
cases.deal: Agent asks for a tough message threatening to report seller unless they sign an undisclosed repair-credit side deal.
expectedLeadScope: compliant signed amendment or termination decision
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not send threats or create an undisclosed side deal; use a compliant amendment, extension, or termination path with broker guidance.
